How to Use the Word Scramble Solver

Using this word unscrambler is straightforward. Type your available letters into the input field and click Solve. The tool will search through a dictionary of over 5,000 common English words and display every valid word that can be formed using your letters. Each letter from your input can only be used once per word (unless it appears multiple times in your input).

For example, if you enter the letters "RETLAS", the solver will find words like "STALER", "ALERTS", "ALTERS", "ASTER", "LATER", "STARE", "TEARS", "RATES", "TALES", "LASER", "SEAL", "SALE", "STAR", "REST", and many more. Results are displayed with their Scrabble point values so you can quickly identify the highest-scoring options.

Using Wildcards

If you have blank tiles or unknown letters, use the question mark (?) character as a wildcard. The solver will try all 26 letters in that position. For instance, entering "CA?" will find CAB, CAD, CAM, CAN, CAP, CAR, CAT, and other three-letter words. Wildcards are worth 0 points in the Scrabble scoring, just like blank tiles in the actual game.

Anagram Mode

Enable anagram mode to find words that use ALL of your input letters exactly once. This is useful when you know the word length and find all possible arrangements. For example, entering "LISTEN" in anagram mode will find "LISTEN", "SILENT", "TINSEL", "ENLIST", and "INLETS".

Scrabble Letter Point Values

The solver calculates Scrabble scores using the official letter values:

  • 1 point: A, E, I, O, U, L, N, S, T, R
  • 2 points: D, G
  • 3 points: B, C, M, P
  • 4 points: F, H, V, W, Y
  • 5 points: K
  • 8 points: J, X
  • 10 points: Q, Z

These values reflect letter rarity in English. Common letters score low while rare letters score high. The solver displays the total score for each word, helping you choose the most valuable play in Scrabble, Words With Friends, and similar games.

Word Game Strategy Tips

Finding words is just the first step. Here are strategies to your score in word games:

  • Look for words that land on premium squares (double/triple letter and word scores). A short word on a triple word score can outscore a long word on regular squares.
  • Use high-value letters (J, X, Q, Z) early when premium squares are still available. Holding them too long can cost you points.
  • Learn two-letter words. Valid two-letter words like QI, XI, ZA, JO, and AX let you play parallel to existing words, scoring in multiple directions at once.
  • Keep a balanced rack. Try to maintain a mix of vowels and consonants. A rack of all vowels or all consonants severely limits your options.
  • Consider the board position. Sometimes a lower-scoring word that blocks your opponent from a premium square is strategically better than a higher-scoring word that opens one up.
  • Save S tiles for strategic plurals. Adding an S to an existing word while forming a new word perpendicular to it gives you points for both words.

Anagram Solving Techniques

Anagrams are words formed by rearranging all the letters of another word or phrase. Solving anagrams is both a useful skill and a fun mental exercise. Here are some techniques:

  • Look for common prefixes and suffixes. Words often start with UN-, RE-, PRE-, or end with -ING, -TION, -ED, -LY. Identifying these patterns narrows down possibilities quickly.
  • Separate vowels and consonants. Write them in two groups and try combining them in different patterns.
  • Look for common letter pairs: TH, SH, CH, QU, CK, NG. These pairs almost always appear together.
  • Try rearranging one letter at a time rather than attempting to solve the entire anagram at once.
  • When stuck, use this solver to find all possible words and discover options you might have missed.

Common Word Patterns

Recognizing common English word patterns helps you spot solutions faster:

  • CVC (consonant-vowel-consonant): cat, dog, pin, set, run
  • band, fast, help, jump, list
  • stop, from, crab, snap, tree
  • CVCE (silent e): make, time, hope, cute, like
  • stand, blend, frost, grant, plumb

About the Dictionary

The -in dictionary contains over 5,000 common English words. It covers everyday vocabulary including common nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and words frequently used in word games. The dictionary is improved for word games and includes most words you would encounter in Scrabble, Words With Friends, and similar games.

Words are validated against this dictionary instantly in your browser. No internet connection is needed after the page loads, and no data is sent to any server. Your searches are completely private.

Using the Results

After solving, you can interact with the results in several ways:

  • Filter by word length using the buttons above the results grid. This is helpful when you need a word with a specific number of letters.
  • Sort results by score (highest first), by length (longest first), or alphabetically.
  • Click any word to see its definition in a popup. Definitions help you verify the word and understand its meaning.
  • Use the "Copy All" button to copy the entire word list to your clipboard for pasting elsewhere.

How does the word scramble solver work?

Enter your scrambled letters and the solver checks all possible combinations against a dictionary of over 5,000 common English words. It finds every valid word that can be formed using your available letters and displays them sorted by length or score.

Can I use wildcard characters?

Yes. Use a question mark (?) to represent an unknown letter. The solver will try all 26 letters in that position to find valid words. You can use multiple wildcards in a single search.

What is the Scrabble score shown next to words?

Each word displays its Scrabble point value based on official letter scores. Common letters like E and A are worth 1 point, while rare letters like Q and Z are worth 10 points. The score helps you choose the highest-value play.

How many words are in the dictionary?

The -in dictionary contains over 5,000 common English words covering everyday vocabulary, common nouns, verbs, adjectives, and words frequently used in word games like Scrabble and Words With Friends.

Can I filter results by word length?

Yes. Use the length filter buttons to show only words of a specific length. This is helpful when you need a word with exactly 4, 5, or 6 letters for a game board or crossword puzzle.

What is an anagram?

An anagram is a word formed by rearranging all the letters of another word. For example, "listen" and "silent" are anagrams of each other. The anagram mode finds words that use ALL of your input letters exactly once.

Does this work for Words With Friends?

Yes. While the scoring system shows Scrabble values, the word finder works for any word game including Words With Friends, Wordle, crossword puzzles, and other letter-based games.

Can I see the definition of a word?

Yes. Click on any word in the results to see its definition. The tool includes basic definitions for common words to help you verify the word and understand its meaning.
